title: One-minute global irradiance of the Baseline Surface Radiation Network (BSRN, ~40 stations, PANGAEA), March, June and December 2019: the length of the day measured
verdict_rule: Days of the same length north and south of the equator at the solstices, or day lengths that a spotlight on the azimuthal-equidistant map reproduces as well as the globe.

sources.cite: A. Driemel et al., Baseline Surface Radiation Network (BSRN): structure and data description (1992-2017), Earth Syst. Sci. Data 10 (2018) 1491-1501; station-month datasets on PANGAEA

units.SWD: W/m², one-minute mean of the downward short-wave irradiance
units.light: minutes per day with SWD >= 5 W/m²
units.day: minutes per day with the Sun's centre above -0.833° (globe)

inputs.origin: PANGAEA, BSRN station-month datasets of March, June and December 2019, found by PANGAEA's search and downloaded as text (fog fetch sun-bsrn).

notes: fog fetch sun-bsrn queries PANGAEA's search for the station-months of March, June and December 2019 and downloads each as text. BSRN conditions of data release apply (bsrn.awi.de). Method: go doc -all ./internal/build/daylen.
public_raw_why: The BSRN conditions of data release ask users not to pass the data on to third parties; get them from PANGAEA.
